localChanges: chore: lock the engine packages that weigh computer players' units against their cities' other needs

log: A Militaristic leader weighs military units 4/3 and a Civilized one 2/3, (3 - Ideology) / 3, mirroring v474.05's improvement weighting. Settlers, Diplomats and Caravans aren't scaled. v474.05 itself scales only improvements, but its scores sit close together; in simple-ai-client's ranking a unit a player needs outscores an improvement it doesn't by more than 4/3, so the lean only acted on about 8 of 1,900 choices until units leant too (civ-clone/web-renderer#378).
core-unit moves from devDependencies to dependencies, and base-unit-type-worker and base-unit-type-diplomatic are added, for the unit classes the rule tells apart.

buildItemInCity keeps one hard rule, a city's own missing defender (wantsUnit). Every other unit quota (explorers, Settlers, attackers, a defender for an undefended city) becomes a score in BuildPriority's scale: policy.needs times how far the player is short of what it wants. Those join the improvements and Wonders ranked by BuildPriority in one ranking (rankWithUnits), each times the leader's BuildWeight, so a leader's lean acts on every choice rather than on a random pick that ran about once in 900 choices (civ-clone/web-renderer#378).

policy.needs: explorer 6 (not weighed by the leader: weighing it cost a seventh of the land explored), settlers 4, attacker 4, reinforcement 3, army 0.09 (an attacker when the player wants no more, just under an everyday improvement), fortification 2 (caps Barracks and City Walls, which civ1-city-improvement scores 100 under threat for cities on Auto), wonder 3 (added to the ruleset's score for the Wonders the AI's own gates allow).
The leader-weighted random pick is gone; nothing in production draws from the random number generator.
The fallback, for a city that needs nothing it can finish soon, now puts units it can support before Barracks and City Walls.

Arena, 80 games x 150 turns against fabfaaf: score +8.2 (t 5.0, mostly Wonders: started 1.5 vs 0.5), cities +0.14 (t 0.7), units lost -3.7 (t -3.6), land explored -11% (t -3.2). With civ1-civilization weighing military units by Ideology, the leader's weighting changes 13% of Civilized leaders' choices (away from attackers) and 5% of Militaristic ones (towards them).

The cap on what Barracks and City Walls score in a city under threat was applied to the score after `BuildWeight`, so every leader's capped at the same 2 and the lean was lost (Copilot, #41). It now caps at `fortification × weight`, i.e. `min(raw, fortification) × weight`.

Weighed, a cap of 2 let a Civilized leader's Barracks (8/3) beat its defenders (3 × 2/3), which cost power (t −2.0), advances (t −2.1) and land explored (t −2.8) against 56e7a63 in 80 arena games. At 1.5 (Civilized 2, Militaristic 1) nothing moves at |t| ≥ 2 against 56e7a63.

The cap test pitted Barracks against a reinforcement, whose score depends on whether civ1-civilization weighs military units (civ-clone/civ1-civilization#2), so it failed on CI, which resolves civ1-civilization from master. An explorer scores the same either way.
The module and `ProductionPolicy` summaries claimed every candidate is weighed by `BuildWeight` and limited by `buildTurns` (Copilot, #41).
